source_text: Proponunt ergo ad suggillandam ignorantiam aliquam apostolorum quod Petrus et qui cum eo reprehensi sunt a Paulo. Adeo, inquiunt, aliquid eis defuit; ut ex hoc etiam illud struant, potuisse postea pleniorem scientiam supervenire, qualis obvenerit Paulo reprehendenti antecessores. Possum et hic Acta Apostolorum repudiantibus dicere: Prius est ut ostendatis quis iste Paulus, et quid ante apostolum, et quomodo apostolus, quatenus et alias ad quaestiones plurimum eo utuntur. Neque enim si ipse se apostolum de persecutore profitetur, sufficit unicuique examinate credenti, quando nec dominus ipse de se testimonium dixerit. Sed credant sine scripturis, ut credant adversus scripturas, tamen doceant ex eo, quod allegant Petrum a Paulo reprehensum, aliam evangelii formam a Paulo superductam citra eam quae praemiserat Petrus et ceteri. Atquin demutatus in praedicatorem de persecutore deducitur ad fratres a fratribus, ut unus ex fratribus, et ad illos ab illis qui ab apostolis fidem induerant. Dehine, sicut ipse enarrat, ascendit in Hierosolyma, cognoscendi Petri causa, ex officio et iure scilicet eiusdem fidei et praedicationis. Nam et illi non essent mirati de persecutore factum praedicatorem, si aliquid contrarium praedicaret, nec dominum praeterea magnificassent, quia adversarius eius Paulus obvenerat. Itaque et dexteram ei dederunt, signum concordiae et convenientiae, et inter se distributionem officii ordinaverunt, non separationem evangelii, nec ut aliud alter, sed ut aliis alter praedicarent, Petrus in circumcisionem. Paulus in nationes. Ceterum si reprehensus est Petrus, quod cum convixisset ethnicis, postea se a convictu eorum separabat personarum respectu, utique conversationis fuit vitium, non praedicationis. Non enim ex hoc alius deus quam creator, et alius Christus quam ex Maria, et alia spes quam resurrectio annuntiabatur.
thought_title: Paul's rebuke of Peter proves no new gospel
orientation: Tertullian is answering heretics who use Paul's rebuke of Peter to claim that the apostles lacked full knowledge and that Paul later brought a fuller gospel.
pass_a_gloss: They put forward therefore, to insult some ignorance of the apostles, the fact that Peter and those who were with him were rebuked by Paul. So much, they say, was lacking to them; so that from this they may also build up that claim, that a fuller knowledge could have arrived afterwards, such as came to Paul when he rebuked his predecessors. I can here also say to those who reject the Acts of the Apostles: It is first necessary that you show who this Paul is, and what he was before being an apostle, and how he became an apostle, since also elsewhere they use him very much for their questions. For neither, if he himself declares himself an apostle from being a persecutor, is that sufficient for anyone who believes with examination, since not even the Lord himself gave testimony about himself. But let them believe without the Scriptures, so that they may believe against the Scriptures; nevertheless let them teach from this, that they allege that Peter was rebuked by Paul, that another form of the gospel was brought in by Paul beyond that which Peter and the others had put forward before. But on the contrary, changed from a persecutor into a preacher, he is led to the brothers by the brothers, as one of the brothers, and to those by those who had put on the faith from the apostles. Then, as he himself relates, he went up to Jerusalem, for the purpose of knowing Peter, by the duty and right, of course, of the same faith and preaching. For they would not have been amazed that a preacher had been made from a persecutor, if he were preaching something contrary, nor would they have glorified the Lord besides, because his adversary Paul had arrived. And so they also gave him the right hand, a sign of concord and agreement, and they arranged between themselves a distribution of the work, not a separation of the gospel, nor so that one might preach one thing, another another thing, but so that one might preach to different people, Peter to the circumcision, Paul to the nations. For the rest, if Peter was rebuked, because when he had lived together with Gentiles, afterwards he separated himself from their company out of respect for persons, it was certainly a fault of conduct, not of preaching. For not from this was another god than the creator, and another Christ than the one from Mary, and another hope than the resurrection being announced.

lemmas.gloss: to put on, to clothe oneself with

choices.why: Keeps the aggressive force of suggillo (to bruise/insult) and the indefinite aliquam, which the heretics allege against the apostles.
Comparative force of pleniorem is essential to the heretics' claim that Paul had more than Peter.

choices.english: for anyone who believes with examination
choices.why: Preserves the unusual adverbial examinate, emphasizing Tertullian's point that belief must be tested, not blind.
Forma is a key technical term here for the shape or character of the gospel message; 'form' keeps the Latin nuance.
Officium here means the assigned task or ministry; 'work' conveys the practical division of labor between Peter and Paul.
This is a literal rendering of the idiom for partiality or favoritism, which is exactly the fault Tertullian attributes to Peter's conduct.

bible_refs.note: Paul rebuked Peter for separating himself from Gentiles out of respect for persons.
Paul went up to Jerusalem to know Peter.
They gave Paul the right hand of fellowship, that he should go to the nations and Peter to the circumcision.

pass_b_english: So to insult some ignorance in the apostles, they bring up the fact that Peter and those with him were rebuked by Paul. "You see," they say, "something was lacking in them." From this they then build the claim that a fuller knowledge could have arrived later, the kind that came to Paul when he rebuked his predecessors. Here too I can say to those who reject the Acts of the Apostles: first you must show who this Paul was, what he was before he became an apostle, and how he became an apostle, since they make heavy use of him in other questions as well. For even if he declares himself an apostle, once a persecutor, that is not enough for anyone who believes with examination, since not even the Lord himself bore witness about himself. But they believe without the Scriptures, so that they believe against the Scriptures. Still, let them prove from what they allege—that Peter was rebuked by Paul—that another form of the gospel was introduced by Paul beyond the one Peter and the rest had delivered before him.

But in fact, changed from a persecutor into a preacher, he is brought to the brothers by the brothers, as one of the brothers, and to those by those who had put on the faith from the apostles. Then, as he himself relates, he went up to Jerusalem to know Peter, from the duty and right, of course, of the same faith and preaching. For they would not have marveled that a persecutor had become a preacher if he were preaching something contrary, nor would they have glorified the Lord because his adversary Paul had come to them. So they gave him the right hand, a sign of concord and agreement, and arranged among themselves a distribution of the work, not a separation of the gospel—not so that one would preach one thing and the other another, but so that one would preach to one group and the other to another: Peter to the circumcision, Paul to the Gentiles.

For the rest, if Peter was rebuked because, after living together with Gentiles, he later separated himself from their company out of respect for persons, that was certainly a fault of conduct, not of preaching. For it was not because of this that another god than the Creator was being announced, or another Christ than the one from Mary, or another hope than the resurrection.

problems.quote: But let them believe without the Scriptures, so that they may believe against the Scriptures.
problems.source_quote: Sed credent sine scripturis, ut credant adversus scripturas
problems.why: Latin states a factual claim (they believe) in indicative; English renders it as an imperative "let them", altering the modality.
problems.fix: But they believe without the Scriptures, so that they believe against the Scriptures.
problems.ruling: Latin 'credent' is indicative ('they believe'), not imperative 'let them believe'; English changes modality from factual claim to command.

edits.old: But let them believe without the Scriptures, so that they may believe against the Scriptures.
edits.new: But they believe without the Scriptures, so that they believe against the Scriptures.

fixed: Changed 'let them believe' to 'they believe' to match the Latin indicative 'credent' and 'credant' (factual statement, not imperative).

problems.why: 'Nations' and 'Gentiles' alternate for the same concept without explanation.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently or note at first occurrence that they are synonymous.

edits.old: Peter to the circumcision, Paul to the nations.
edits.new: Peter to the circumcision, Paul to the Gentiles.

fixed: The glossary problem about 'nations' and 'Gentiles' alternating is valid: the source uses 'nationes' for the same group rendered as 'Gentiles' earlier in the sentence ('after living together with Gentiles'). Using 'Gentiles' consistently resolves the unexplained alternation.

last_rejected.quote: So to insult some ignorance in the apostles,
last_rejected.source_quote: Proponunt ergo ad suggillandam ignorantiam aliquam apostolorum
last_rejected.why: Latin says they propose to expose or sharpen some ignorance of the apostles, not to insult them; agency and tone are changed.
last_rejected.fix: So they propose to expose some ignorance of the apostles,
last_rejected.ruling: suggillandam can mean 'to expose/ridicule'; 'insult' is within range. Not a major meaning change.
